subject: Performance SLO benchmark methodology & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@edgefin.com>, Nora Alvarez <nora@edgefin.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO benchmark methodology & next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Per our call, I wanted to capture the performance / SLO targets you outlined and propose a concrete benchmark methodology we can run for EdgeFin to validate feasibility and sizing. Please review below and flag anything missing.

Recap of targets (from discovery):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end inference latency target <= 150 ms for standard (non-streaming) text-generation endpoints
- Streaming: p95 token-level latency target <= 80 ms for streaming chat flows (token-by-token delivery)
- Throughput: sustained throughput target ~500 req/s for peak windows (mixed short/long prompts)
- Concurrency: up to 200 concurrent active sessions (mix of streaming + non-streaming)
- Accuracy / quality: use your provided prompt set (attached) and our eval harness to ensure outputs match baseline acceptance criteria

Benchmark artifacts attached: redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.pdf (methodology summary) and edgefin_prompt_set_v2.csv (120 prompts across short/long/chat).

Proposed measurement approach (high level):
- Deterministic generation config (temp=0, top_k fixed) for reproducibility unless you request sampling tests
- Warmup phase (1000 requests) before measurements to populate KV cache and eliminate cold-start variance
- Measure both inference-only (server-side processing) and end-to-end (client-observed) latencies; report p50/p90/p95/p99 and token-level streaming times
- Run 5 iterations over the full prompt set to capture variance; provide raw traces and aggregated stats

Questions / asks from your side:
1) Can you confirm whether you want the benchmark run in EdgeFin's cloud account (we can run in your test project/VPC) or using Redwood-hosted infra for an initial proof?
2) Please share any network egress constraints, peering details, or fixed IP allowlists we should use.
3) Confirm the production-like prompt set and any sensitive prompts that should be excluded.

Next steps:
- If we have permission to run in your test account, share temporary creds + brief network details by Mon 6/29 so we can schedule kickoff
- Proposed kickoff: Wed 6/30 10:00 AM PT — 30m sync to validate config and kick the run
- Deliverables: methodology doc, raw traces, aggregated SLO report, and a reproducibility checklist (attached).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@edgefin.com>

Date: 2026-06-26T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology & next steps

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A few quick clarifications before we turn over creds: 

- When you say p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 150 ms, do you mean inference-only (server processing time) or end-to-end client-observed (including network + SDK)? We need both numbers but want to understand your default reporting.
- For streaming token latency, can you confirm how token delivery time is measured (server send vs client receive)? We have some internal buffering and sdk-level batching that can affect numbers.
- Preference: we'd prefer Redwood run the initial benchmark in our test AWS account (sandbox) so results include our network/topology. We'll provide a temporary IAM role if that works.

I'll loop in Nora for any network requirements. Also please include cold-start vs warm-start breakdowns in the report — those are important for our on-call SLAs.

One more ask — can you share the script names and the assumption of deterministic config so we can vet them?

On Wed 6/30 10am PT works for a kickoff.

Best,
Sanjay
VP Product, EdgeFin
sanjay.patel@edgefin.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@edgefin.com>
Date: 2026-06-27T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology & next steps

Adding specifics on the benchmark methodology and the scripts we'll run so Sanjay/Nora have full visibility before we get credentials. Short version up top, full details below.

Measurement definitions (what we'll report):
- Cold-start latency: first request latency after process/container start (we'll report distribution across containers)
- Warm-start latency: latency after a warmup window (we'll use 1k requests as Marissa suggested)
- End-to-end: measured at the client (timestamp request send -> client receives final token). We will also report server-side inference-only (time spent in model forward + decode) to separate network impact
- Token-level streaming latency: time from server-side token emission to client-side receipt; we will instrument our harness to timestamp tokens on emit and on client recv for accurate delta

Experiment configuration (defaults unless you ask otherwise):
- Sampling: deterministic (temperature=0, top_k=40) for reproducibility; we can add sampling experiments afterward
- Model config: max_tokens=256, stop sequences per prompt as provided, beam/greedy set to default (deterministic generation)
- Concurrency ramp: linear ramp to target concurrency over 2 min, sustain for 10 min, cool-down 2 min; repeat 3 runs per configuration
- Iterations: 5 full iterations over your prompt set
- Warmup: first 1k requests excluded from measurement, then measurement window begins

Reproducibility and artifacts we will produce:
- Exact harness commit hash and container image tag (we pin both in the report); harness lives at https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness
- The run script names: run_edgefin_benchmark.sh, collect_traces.py, aggregate_slo_report.py
- Raw traces (per-request JSON lines), aggregated summary (csv + xlsx), and a reproducibility checklist with container image + seeds + command-line args

Streaming-specific notes:
- To capture token-level latency, we instrument both sides and recommend running with an SDK that streams immediately to the client (no client-side buffering). We'll include a small client shim if your current SDK buffers by default.

Security note: if we run in your AWS account we'll ask for a temporary IAM role with least-privilege and a short TTL; if we run in Redwood-hosted infra we'll provide an enclave-style test run and additional network/perf caveats.

I'll attach a short methodology appendix and the harness README to the hub. Happy to adjust any parameter.

--
Aditya Rao
